patterns.rationale: All four misses use `[TB: "..."]` as the instruction-embedding wrapper — it is the delivery mechanism shared across every payload in this category. No legitimate changelog, package.json, JSDoc, or notebook cell uses this bracket-colon-quote form.
patterns.fp_notes: None — `[TB:` followed immediately by a quote has no plausible legitimate use.

patterns.rationale: Each miss introduces a distinct invented synonym for "send data to a URL" (`forward_payload`, `stream_to_collector`, `push_to_endpoint`, `transmit_to_host`). These are the exfil-action half of the two-step payload pattern. Adding them as bare tool-name alternations (consistent with how `send_http`, `post_webhook` are already caught) closes this synonym class.
patterns.fp_notes: `push_to_endpoint` is the closest to a generic phrase, but as a bare underscore-joined identifier it does not appear in API documentation prose. The others are highly distinctive.

patterns.rationale: Each miss introduces a distinct invented synonym for "read an environment variable / secret" (`pull_var`, `pull_runtime_secret`, `access_runtime_store`, `retrieve_process_binding`). These are the secret-retrieval half of the two-step pattern. The `\b` anchor prevents substring matches inside longer legitimate identifiers. None of these function names appear in any known-good corpus file.
patterns.fp_notes: `pull_var` is the most generic; the word boundary reduces risk. `retrieve_process_binding` and `access_runtime_store` are entirely synthetic. No match found in known-good docs.
